Posterior shoulder dislocation: 2

An axial image confirms posterior shoulder dislocation and an impaction defect in the anteromedial humeral head. The defect differs in location from that associated with anterior dislocation. Which named lesion best describes this finding?

  1. Bankart lesion
  2. Hill-Sachs lesion
  3. Rotator cuff tear
  4. Recurrent instability
  5. Reverse Hill-Sachs lesion
Answer and explanation

Reverse Hill-Sachs lesion

Posterior dislocation may cause an anteromedial humeral head impaction defect.

Option explanations

Reverse Hill-Sachs lesion: Posterior dislocation may cause an anteromedial humeral head impaction defect.

Bankart lesion: A Bankart lesion involves the anteroinferior glenoid labrum, commonly after anterior dislocation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Hill-Sachs lesion: An anterior dislocation may impact the posterolateral humeral head against the glenoid rim. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Rotator cuff tear: Persistent weakness after reduction, especially in older patients, warrants assessment for associated cuff injury. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Recurrent instability: Capsulolabral injury can predispose to recurrent glenohumeral dislocation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
